newsitem.title: GERMANY: Varta sells Brazil unit to BTR.
newsitem.headline: Varta sells Brazil unit to BTR.

text.p: German battery maker Varta AG said on Thursday it would sell its industrial battery operations in Brazil to British conglomerate BTR Plc for $72 million.
Varta's Microlite SA unit of Sao Paulo would concentrate on batteries for portable electronics, while BTR would operate the industrial business under the name Saturnia Hawker Sistemas de Energia.
Varta sells Brazil unit to BTR
The industrial business had 1996 sales of $67 million, and was expected to reach $100 million in sales this year, Varta said.
Microlite, which Varta took over at the beginning of the year, had 1996 sales of $136 million and controlled 50 percent of the Brazilian market for portable batteries.
In 1995, BTR bought Varta's European industrial battery operations.

On July 23, Varta said it would close a plant in the United States that it had opened a year ago in a venture with Gillette Co.'s Duracell unit and Toshiba Corp. The firms were keeping the alliance but moved production to Japan to reduce costs.
Varta also forecast it would turn a profit in the year ending September 30 after five years of losses. In 1995/96, it lost 25 million marks on sales of 1.99 billion marks.
BTR's 1996 pre-tax profit fell 13 percent to 1.3 billion stg, although sales rose 10.5 percent to 8.4 billion stg.
